messages:
incident-bot: [P1] ALERT — multiple containers restarting in us-west-2-prod serving pool (gpu-rt). Symptoms: repeated container restarts, elevated 5xxs, and CUDA errors in logs. Pager -> maya, sahil. Please ack and triage.

maya: acked. I'm on it. seeing spikes in prefill memory usage in the runtime metrics dashboard.

sahil: ack. grabbing logs and node list now. can someone post the exact error lines?

maya: logs from one pod: ```
[2026-03-14T22:09:12Z] runtime: prefill allocate 1.4G tokens -> OOM
[2026-03-14T22:09:12Z] runtime: CUDA error on device 0: cudaErrorIllegalAddress
[2026-03-14T22:09:12Z] containerd: container "model-runner-abc" exited with status 137 (killed)
```

liam: that looks like prefill blowup from a huge context. metrics show a tail of requests with context_length > 200k tokens in the last 7m.

maya: confirmed. top offending route: /v1/generate (customer: fin-analytics-prod). Percentile breakdown: p99 context size ~ 185k tokens, average prefill gpu mem per req ~ 11.2GB -> pushes container over limits on many nodes.

eva: CS note — I just messaged the customer (FinAnalytics) and they report long system prompts + document upload causing timeouts. They see 503s starting ~22:07. Keeping them updated.

sahil: immediate mitigations we can do: 1) apply runtime guard to trim prefill > 32k tokens 2) route FinAnalytics to small-quantized model variant (less memory) 3) drain most impacted nodes and restart pods 4) scale up extra GPU capacity if needed. Which one do we execute first?

maya: do 1 and 2 now. I'll push a temporary config to limit prefill tokens and enable early-kv-eviction flag.

deploy-bot: maya triggered change: PATCH /runtime/config - {"prefill_max_tokens": 32768, "enable_prefill_eviction": true} (applied to pool gpu-rt-usw2-prod)

maya: change applied. confirming via metrics. prefill requests above 32k are now being truncated at ingress.

sahil: routing change applied to FinAnalytics: traffic -> model-gpt-4o-quant-small (fallback). Verify if that reduces OOMs.

liam: after the trim + fallback, error rate fell ~60% in 3m. however we still see sporadic restarts on two nodes with older drivers (NVIDIA 515). kernel logs show occasional 'device-side assert' around the same time.

maya: I'm going to cordon those two nodes and rotate pods off them. starting drain now: `kubectl drain gpu-node-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

incident-bot: ACTIONS LOGGED — cordon/drain in progress by maya.

sahil: also triggered a short autoscale bump: +2 gpus to the pool to relieve pressure.

deploy-bot: autoscale: scaled pool gpu-rt-usw2-prod from 8 -> 10 gpus (requested by sahil).

eva: customer update sent — FinAnalytics saw degraded performance for ~14 minutes; they are ok with fallback to a smaller model for now. Asking for timeline on full fix.

maya: post-hotfix checks: no new restarts in the last 6 minutes on control plane metrics. prefill evictions are firing, trimmed requests show reduced GPU RAM usage.

liam: we'll need a follow-up: 1) block super-long contexts at API gateway (hard limit at 100k tokens) 2) patch runtime to cap internal prefill allocations earlier and add protective OOM-rescue where prefill allocation can be rejected gracefully not crash container 3) upgrade driver on affected nodes to NVIDIA driver 535 and repro test.

sahil: logging a ticket for runtime-hotfix: RUNTIME-4621. assigning to eng-runtime. initial priority P1.

maya: temporary mitigation summary for postmortem: - ingress prefill trim (32k) - customer routing to quantized fallback - node drain and driver upgrade plan - autoscale bump - customer notified by CS.

eva: customer impact: FinAnalytics had 503s for 14 minutes, no data loss reported. They were routed to smaller model which returned slower but successful results. CSA will follow up to support config changes on their side to limit upload sizes.

liam: root-cause hypothesis: lack of defensive prefill limits + a small but real population of requests that include huge user-supplied documents. This combined with older driver instability produced OOMs and device-side errors leading to container kills.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS -> mitigated (11:39 UTC: rate of restarts back to baseline). On-call: maya, sahil, liam to do triage and postmortem.

maya: creating postmortem draft and linking runbook items. Will include timeline, mitigations, and long-term fixes (gateway hard limit, runtime allocation cap, better metrics/alerts on prefill size).

sahil: will follow up with eng-infra to schedule controlled driver rollout for the fleet and add test coverage for large prefill cases.

eva: I'll coordinate customer follow-up and schedule a joint call if they want deeper assistance.

liam: final note — collect full set of offending request IDs for the last hour so cs can correlate with customer logs. I'll run a query and paste results into the postmortem.

maya: thanks all. closing pager and will hand to postmortem owners. :white_check_mark:
